text:
olivia: acme-sec just DM'd us — their storage-monitor flagged a public S3 bucket that appears to contain our telemetry logs (partial user ids). unsure if any API keys or secrets exposed. can someone own this?

samir: I own the integration with ACME. which bucket path?

olivia: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/buckets/acme-shared-telemetry?prefix=redwood-prod-telemetry-2026 — detector shows ~8k objects, last modified yesterday, severity: medium.

sec-bot: alert from storage-monitor: public_object_put detected (rule: public-s3-objects), id: alert-4439.

jess: do we know if objects are SSE-KMS/encrypted with our CMK or vendor-managed key? need KMS decrypt logs + CloudTrail to assess exposure.

samir: looks like SSE-KMS -> KeyId: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111222333:alias/acme-logs-key (vendor-managed). not our CMK. I don't see our account as key user.

mike: ok. that reduces risk of key compromise, but still risk if files contain API tokens/IDs. can you grab a sample of 10 objects and grep for suspicious strings? don't download everything.

samir: running a sample pull now. snippet:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://acme-shared-telemetry/redwood-prod-telemetry-2026/sample-0001.gz - | zcat | head -n 100
```

samir: sample output: `{"event":"page_view","user_id_partial":"u_7a3f..","session_id":"s-xx-yy","metadata":{}}` — no clear API keys in first 100 lines, but there are user identifiers truncated.

olivia: vendor says they didn't intend to make bucket public; acme-sec: can you confirm when ACL was public and what objects were exposed? we need a timeline for comms. :eyes: @acme-sec

acme-sec: we found misconfigured lifecycle job that re-copied objects to a public prefix between 2026-04-22 02:15 and 2026-04-22 08:40 UTC. ACL set to public-read during that window; we have revoked the ACL and are running re-encryption. will share manifest of objects affected in 15m.

jess: please open an incident (SOC) and include manifest. I want CloudTrail S3:GetObject logs + KMS:Decrypt attempts during window, and any referrals in WAF/edge logs. legal should be looped for data classification.

mike: temporary containment: i've requested ACME to remove public-read and added a bucket policy to deny GetObject for Principal = * until we validate. also adding a CloudWatch Alarm for s3:ObjectAclChanged and a CloudTrail filter.

samir: performed quick check: no KMS:Decrypt by unknown principals in that timeframe. looks like objects were readable without decrypt because SSE-KMS still allows GetObject if authorized; the public ACL was the issue.

olivia: good. follow-up actions: 1) vendor to provide manifest and retention/remediation plan, 2) we require proof that no secrets present (sample audit), 3) update vendor onboarding checklist to require KMS ownership verification and a post-deploy ACL scan, 4) add alert for public object put and lifecycle copy jobs.

sec-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0423 (severity: medium). assigned: samir, jess, mike, olivia.

mike: I pushed a short-lived RBAC lock: blocked the IAM role used by acme for ListBucket/ListObjects in our prefix (policy ID: tmp-block-1792109915). will revert after vendor confirms cleanup.

samir: vendor manifest attached in DM, sample looks like mostly telemetry. no API keys found in spot check but we should run a regex scan over full manifest. I'll run that and post results.

olivia: thanks. we'll do a post-incident review tomorrow 10:00am PT to formalize changes (onboarding checklist, RBAC gating, CloudTrail + KMS log retention). jess — can you handle SOC/Legal ping and draft a short customer-facing blurb if needed?

jess: on it. drafting incident summary and legal classification now. will escalate if we find PII.

olivia: great. notes: add automated test in CI for vendor integrations that rejects public ACLs and enforces KMS alias owner check.

sec-bot: note: evidence artifacts uploaded to secure-bucket/incidents/INC-2026-0423/ (access: security-team only).

olivia: assigning follow-ups: samir (full regex scan + confirm no keys), jess (incident report + legal loop), mike (RBAC + alert tuning), acme-sec (manifest + remediation verification). syncing tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
